notes: runtime_s times composite() only (all years for one place); load_s is np.load of the cached npz.

composite_peak_alloc_mb is tracemalloc peak inside composite() (includes the 43-year uint16 output, ~27 MB); peak_process_memory_mb is the whole-process peak working set, dominated by the decompressed scene cache.
Only the K(K-1)/2 pairs i<j are computed; a first version with a full [K,K,H,W] matrix took ~7-10 s per place at N=6, this one ~2.6-3.4 s.

Scenes per year are ordered by cloud_cover ascending, so argmin's first-index tie-break gives the 2-observation rule (lower cloud_cover wins) and also breaks rarer exact ties among 3+ observations the same way.

Self-test (python composite.py --test) covers outlier rejection, 1/2/0 clear observations, masked observations, the cloud_cover tie-break through composite(), fill pixels (qa=1, dn=0) and saturated (65535) bands.

Mask uses the corrected rule: invalid if qa==0, any of bits 0-5 set, or any reflectance band is 0 or 65535. Outputs were regenerated after the correction (the first rule let qa=1 fill pixels through as all-zero observations).
Timings measured while other S2 spike agents may have been running in parallel; treat as upper bounds.
problems: With 2 clear observations the medoid cannot reject an outlier: it is just the lower-cloud scene, so N=2 behaves like best-scene with per-pixel fallback; a missed cloud in that scene passes through.
